solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet's slack about vacuous rhymes

indicators.note: about tells us the slackening word goes round the emptied word

parts.note: to veer a rope is to slacken it, a nautical sense

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied of contents, leaving only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A poet is told off for loose, empty verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just a link (is) between definition and wordplay; veer as slacken is a sailing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A verser is an old word for a versifier, someone who writes verse.

clue.text: Caesar's force surrounding chariot substitutes

indicators.note: surrounding means the Latin word is placed around the vehicle

parts.note: vis is the Latin word for force, as Caesar would say
a chariot is a car in older usage

explanation.surface: Roman military might encircling a war chariot.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicars are deputies standing in for someone else, from Latin vicarius, a substitute.

clue.text: Loosely insist one will include a litotes, say

indicators.note: will include means the anagram takes the letter inside it
loosely means the letters of the two words are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a figure of understatement should be counted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loosely' rearranges INSIST ONE and 'will include' slips A in among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enantiosis is a figure of speech saying something by denying its opposite, and litotes is an example.

clue.text: Ship's timber springs about

parts.note: springs from means stems from, so springs gives the verb stems
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A ship's timbers spring around as it rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemson is a curved piece of timber in a ship's bow, fixed behind the stem.

clue.text: Mostly such as Hemingway, those that will feed on fish

definitions.text: those that will feed on fish

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Hemingway's first name, Ernest, is a name such as his

explanation.surface: Hemingway and his kind were keen fishermen, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Hemingway was a famous angler, which makes the fish-eating definition sound like part of the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, birds that catch and eat fish.

clue.text: Substantial lead of observant German politician

parts.note: substantial means real, actually existing

indicators.note: lead of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An attentive politician gives a solid lead.
explanation.walkthrough: A Realo is a member of the pragmatic wing of the German Green Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Realo is the term for a realist, moderate member of Germany's Greens, as opposed to a Fundi.

clue.text: Berliner's one back behind little banger

parts.note: wee is Scots for little

indicators.note: back means the German word is read from right to left

parts.note: ein is German for one, as said in Berlin

explanation.surface: A German watches a small firework go off behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, not a firework here.
explanation.definitionFit: A weenie is a frankfurter or sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Contend with what's inside deadly hard antipodean shrub

parts.note: to war is to fight or contend

indicators.note: what's inside means the middle of the word, its ends lost

parts.note: deadly means fatal
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Struggling with a dangerous, tough Australian bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The waratah is an Australian shrub with red flower heads, the emblem of New South Wales.

clue.text: Bolt upright round end of parade

indicators.note: round means the post word is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: an upright is a pole or post

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of parade

explanation.surface: A soldier stands bolt upright at the end of a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt upright' reads as one phrase, but Bolt is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly with a lover, to bolt.

clue.text: Who hoarded treasure? Point east over town's open area

parts.note: a nib is a point, as of a pen
a park is called a lung of a town, an open space letting it breathe

explanation.surface: Asking who hid a hoard, then giving map directions to a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' just places the pieces one above the other in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Germanic legend the Nibelungs were a race of dwarfs who guarded a treasure hoard.

clue.text: Right away Scottish professor's office finds need

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a regency was the office of a regent, a teacher in a Scottish university

explanation.surface: A Scottish academic finds his post gone immediately when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Egency is a rare word for want or necessity.

clue.text: Rest easily in the morning and fish burn

indicators.note: easily means the letters are loosely rearranged

parts.note: AM means in the morning
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Lie in, then go fishing in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is the Scots word for a stream, not a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamling is a small stream or rivulet, like a burn.

clue.text: Old dainty locally not of a chain

parts.note: a cate is an archaic word for a dainty or delicacy
nary is dialect for not or never a

explanation.surface: An old local cake is not part of a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Catenary describes the curve of a hanging chain, from Latin catena.

clue.text: Crown and Dieu, core grouping for Jacques de Molay's sincere appeal (10, three words)

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown

indicators.note: grouping means the letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Royal and divine words at the heart of a Templar's last plea.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques de Molay was the last Grand Master of the Templars, a Frenchman, hence the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A cri de coeur is a passionate heartfelt appeal, literally a cry of the heart in French.

clue.text: Adult programme from city in southern France, nearly

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Nimes is a city in the south of France

explanation.surface: An adult show from Provence, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult programme' looks like the definition, but Adult gives only A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is Japanese animated film or television, a kind of programme.

clue.text: River vertebrate to run wild in the Highlands and, well, north

parts.words: to run wild in the Highlands
parts.note: lamp is a Scots verb meaning to scamper or run wild
er is a hesitation, like well

explanation.surface: A Highland river creature runs wild, heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: The lampern is the river lamprey, an eel-like fish with a backbone.

clue.text: In full agreement, university's playing a lecturer

parts.note: uni is short for university, with the possessive s
on means playing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A university orchestra plays with a lecturer joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisonal means sounding in unison, completely in accord.

clue.text: Catholic circling priest's monument

indicators.note: circling means the abbreviation goes around the priest's name

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli was the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A Catholic shrine surrounds a priest's tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, a memorial or monument.

clue.text: Drawing of dutiful female after forgotten shame

indicators.note: after puts the female word and its partner behind the word for shame

parts.note: sin is an old word for shame, one now forgotten
o' is a short form of of
pia is the Latin feminine for dutiful or pious

explanation.surface: A sketch of a devoted woman who has put a disgrace behind her.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinopia is the reddish underdrawing for a fresco, a preparatory sketch.

clue.text: Mineral in cool box

parts.note: to ice is to cool
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: Minerals kept in a cool box.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice spar is a clear glassy form of feldspar, a mineral.

clue.text: Grand drunken day around university?

indicators.note: around means the letters for day are placed about the university letter
drunken means the letters of the word are reeled about

explanation.surface: A big boozy day out at college.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a college feast, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaudy is a feast or reunion dinner held at an Oxford or Cambridge college.

clue.text: Judge being trapped by attorney basically

indicators.note: being trapped by means the judging word goes inside

parts.note: Att. is the abbreviation for attorney
to hear a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A judge caught by a lawyer at bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally or in essence, which is basically.

clue.text: Rendering acupressure on back of leg

parts.note: do-in is a Japanese self-massage form of acupressure

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of leg

explanation.surface: Treating a leg with pressure points.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing means performing or rendering, as a rendering of a song is a doing of it.

clue.text: Plan to remove immorality whimsically

definitions.meaning: a jokey verb meaning to take away the vice from something

explanation.definitionFit: A device is a plan or scheme, and de-vice whimsically means remove vice.

clue.text: Relish chart as backing desire

parts.note: ch. is an abbreviation for chart
ut is Latin for as

indicators.note: backing means the craving word is read from the end

parts.note: a yen is a desire

explanation.surface: Plotting relish on a graph as a fond wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutney is a spicy condiment, a type of relish.

clue.text: Term for anniversary, soon to be like birthdays perhaps

indicators.note: term means end, so the last letter of anniversary

parts.note: early means soon

explanation.surface: Anniversary celebrations coming round early, like birthdays.
explanation.definitionFit: Birthdays come once a year, so they are annual occurrences.

clue.text: Try filling-free eclairs, for example

indicators.note: filling-free means the middle is removed, keeping only the outer letters

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: Sample some unfilled pastries, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, and to essay is to try.

clue.text: End of raga to readily take in a start of raga

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of raga

parts.note: to lap up is to take in eagerly

explanation.surface: Ending and beginning a raga in the same breath.
explanation.definitionFit: An alapa is the slow improvised opening section of a raga.

clue.text: Is small flock of wildfowl clear?

parts.note: 's is a contraction of is
a trip is a small flock of wildfowl

explanation.surface: Is a small group of ducks gone?
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to clear away or empty out something completely.

clue.text: Whitening could be a humiliation for Macron

parts.note: gene is French for embarrassment, as the French president would say

explanation.surface: A whitening scandal could embarrass the French president.
explanation.definitionFit: Agene is nitrogen trichloride, once used to bleach flour white.

clue.text: Musician: see one duck choice

parts.note: v. is short for vide, Latin for see
I is the Roman numeral one
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, looking like O
list is an archaic word for choice or desire

explanation.surface: A musician sees a duck and makes a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A violist is a player of the viola or viol.

clue.text: Against, for example, returning a sail

indicators.note: returning means both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: on means against, as leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: Returning a sail, against advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A genoa is a large jib sail on a yacht.

clue.text: Who unfolds special pocketbook?

parts.note: reader is old thieves' slang for a pocketbook

explanation.surface: Asking who opens a special wallet.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreader is one who spreads or unfolds something.

clue.text: Fastidious about simple Christian office

indicators.note: about means the cautious word goes around the plain one

parts.note: chary means cautious or fastidious
plain means simple

explanation.surface: A fussy person reviews a simple church job.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplainry is the office or post of a chaplain.

clue.text: Nut to go to ground like Blériot at his finest moment

definitions.text: like Blériot at his finest moment

parts.note: in printing an en is called a nut
to lair is to go to one's den

explanation.surface: A crank goes into hiding, while the pioneer aviator flies.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis Blériot was first to fly the English Channel, in 1909, so in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: En l'air is French for in the air, where an aviator is at his finest.

clue.text: Indulge with answer those at the heart of worrying source of fuel

parts.note: to pet is to indulge or pamper

indicators.note: those at the heart of means the central letters of worrying

explanation.surface: Coddling with answers to fuel a worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A petary is a peat bog, where turf for burning is cut.
